lessons.summary: Join a family dinner at Grandma’s and say the right things at the table.

content.title: Family dinner
content.scenario: Join a family dinner at Grandma’s and say the right things at the table.

rounds.situation: Grandma has finished cooking. Call everyone to the table.
rounds.jyutping: maa4 maa4 giu3 daai6 gaa1 sik6 faan6 laa1
rounds.translation: Grandma says it’s time to eat, everyone!

chunks.note: 嫲嫲 is your dad’s mum; your mum’s mum is 婆婆.
啦 turns it into a warm, friendly nudge.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Call the family to the table for Grandma.

rounds.situation: Before you pick up your chopsticks, invite each elder to eat.
rounds.jyutping: maa4 maa4 sik6 faan6 je4 je2 sik6 faan6
rounds.translation: Grandma, please eat. Grandpa, please eat.

chunks.note: Kids invite every elder by name before they start. Elders notice!
Go from oldest to youngest.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite Grandma and Grandpa to start eating.

rounds.situation: You taste Grandma’s slow-cooked soup.
rounds.jyutping: ni1 go3 tong1 hou2 hou2 jam2 aa3
rounds.translation: This soup is so good!

chunks.note: Soup comes first at a Cantonese family dinner.
Soup is drunk, so it’s 好飲, not 好食.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Compliment Grandma’s soup.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: ni1 go3 tong1 hou2 hou2 jam2 aa3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: This soup is so good!

options.englishTranslation: This soup is too salty.
This soup is so good!
I can’t eat any more, I’m so full.

rounds.situation: Grandma keeps putting food in your bowl.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 sik6 m4 lok6 laa3 hou2 baau2 aa3
rounds.translation: I can’t eat any more, I’m so full.

chunks.note: 喇 signals a change: you were hungry, now you’re not.
Say it with a smile. Grandma will try anyway.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Politely tell Grandma you’re full.

rounds.situation: Leaving after dinner, promise to come back.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 zoi3 lai4 sik6
rounds.translation: I’ll come eat again next week!

chunks.note: Put the time before the action.
嚟 means come. It’s the best goodbye at Grandma’s.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Promise Grandma you’ll come back next week.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: ngo5 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 zoi3 lai4 sik6
responseExercise.promptTranslation: I’ll come eat again next week!

options.englishTranslation: Grandma says it’s time to eat, everyone!
This soup is so good!
I’ll come eat again next week!

lessons.summary: Chat with a friend about a café and sound natural with sentence-final particles.

content.title: The particles
content.scenario: Chat with a friend about a café and sound natural with sentence-final particles.

rounds.situation: You tell a friend about a café you love.
rounds.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 cafe hou2 zeng3 gaa3
rounds.translation: This café is really great, you know!

chunks.note: Locals just say cafe in English.
㗎 adds confidence: you’re vouching for it.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Recommend your favourite café.

rounds.situation: Your friend says they’ve never been. You’re surprised.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3 me1
rounds.translation: You haven’t been? Really?

chunks.note: 未 means not yet, so there’s still hope.
咩 at the end turns it into a surprised question.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Act surprised that your friend hasn’t been.

rounds.situation: Suggest going together.
rounds.jyutping: gam2 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 laa1
rounds.translation: Then let’s go together.

chunks.note: 咁 links your idea to what was just said.
啦 makes it a friendly suggestion, not an order.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest going to the café together.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: gam2 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 laa1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Then let’s go together.

options.englishTranslation: You haven’t been? Really?
Let’s go tomorrow without them.
Then let’s go together.

rounds.situation: Pass on what you heard about their egg tarts.
rounds.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 di1 daan6 taat1 hou2 hou2 sik6 wo3
rounds.translation: Apparently their egg tarts are really good.

chunks.note: 啲 works like the for plural things.
喎 passes on something you heard or just noticed.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Share what you heard about their egg tarts.

rounds.situation: Wrap up the plan.
rounds.jyutping: hou2 laa1 ting1 jat6 gin3 lo1
rounds.translation: Alright, see you tomorrow then.

chunks.note: 好啦 closes a discussion warmly.
囉 means it’s settled, nothing more to say.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Agree and say see you tomorrow.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: hou2 laa1 ting1 jat6 gin3 lo1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Alright, see you tomorrow then.

options.englishTranslation: Alright, see you tomorrow then.

lessons.summary: Swap weekend stories on Monday: what you did, what you’re planning and what you’ve tried.

content.title: Your weekend
content.scenario: Swap weekend stories on Monday: what you did, what you’re planning and what you’ve tried.

rounds.situation: It’s Monday. Ask your friend about their weekend.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 zau1 mut6 zou6 zo2 di1 me1 aa3
rounds.translation: What did you do on the weekend?

chunks.note: Time words go near the start.
咗 after a verb means it’s done.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask what your friend did on the weekend.

rounds.situation: They ask you back. Tell them about your Sunday.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 heoi3 zo2 haang4 saan1
rounds.translation: I went hiking.

chunks.note: Same 咗: the trip is finished.
Literally walk the mountain. A Hong Kong weekend favourite.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you went hiking.

rounds.situation: Ask if they know the famous trail you did.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 haang4 gwo3 lung4 zek3 mei6 aa3
rounds.translation: Have you ever hiked Dragon’s Back?

chunks.note: 過 after a verb means ever done it.
Verb + 過 … 未 asks have you ever?

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask if your friend has ever hiked Dragon’s Back.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: nei5 haang4 gwo3 lung4 zek3 mei6 aa3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Have you ever hiked Dragon’s Back?

options.englishTranslation: I went hiking.
Do you want to hike Dragon’s Back today?
Have you ever hiked Dragon’s Back?

rounds.situation: They haven’t. Share your next plan.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 nam2 gan2 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 zoi3 heoi3
rounds.translation: I’m thinking of going again next week.

chunks.note: 緊 after a verb means it’s happening right now.

chunks.jyutping: haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 zoi3 heoi3
chunks.note: 再 means again.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you’re thinking of going again next week.

rounds.situation: Convince your friend to come along.
rounds.jyutping: nei5 mei6 haang4 gwo3 jat1 ding6 jiu3 si3 haa5
rounds.translation: If you’ve never done it, you have to try it.

chunks.note: 未 + verb + 過: never done it so far.
下 after a verb makes it casual: just give it a go.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell your friend they have to try the hike.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: nei5 mei6 haang4 gwo3 jat1 ding6 jiu3 si3 haa5
responseExercise.promptTranslation: If you’ve never done it, you have to try it.

options.englishTranslation: If you’ve never done it, you have to try it.
I’m thinking of going again next week.
You’ve done it already, no need to go again.

lessons.summary: Ask someone out to a movie, set the time and place, and book the tickets.

content.title: Making plans
content.scenario: Ask someone out to a movie, set the time and place, and book the tickets.

rounds.situation: Ask your date if they’re free this weekend.
rounds.cantonese: 你今個禮拜六得唔得閒呀？
rounds.jyutping: nei5 gam1 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 aa3
rounds.translation: Are you free this Saturday?

chunks.jyutping: nei5 gam1 go3 lai5 baai3 luk6
chunks.note: 禮拜 + number gives the weekday. 六 is Saturday.
得閒 means free; 得唔得閒 asks it as yes or no.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask if they’re free this Saturday.

rounds.situation: They are! Say what you have in mind.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 joek3 nei5 heoi3 tai2 hei3
rounds.translation: I’d like to take you to a movie.

chunks.english: I’d like to ask you out
chunks.note: 約 is to make a date with someone.
睇戲 literally means watch a show.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite them to a movie.

rounds.situation: Set the time and the meeting point.
rounds.jyutping: cat1 dim2 bun3 hai2 wong6 gok3 dang2 laa1
rounds.translation: Let’s meet in Mong Kok at 7:30.

chunks.note: 點 is o’clock, 半 is half.
Hong Kongers say wait for, not meet.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest a time and place to meet.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: cat1 dim2 bun3 hai2 wong6 gok3 dang2 laa1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Let’s meet in Mong Kok at 7:30.

options.englishTranslation: Let’s meet in Mong Kok at 7:30.
Let’s meet in Central at 8:30.
I’d like to take you to a movie.

rounds.situation: Let them know the tickets are sorted.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 book zo2 hei3 fei1 laa3
rounds.translation: I’ve booked the tickets.

chunks.note: Locals mix in English verbs like book, then add 咗.
飛 is the everyday word for ticket.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you’ve already booked the tickets.

rounds.situation: One last thing before you hang up.
rounds.jyutping: ci4 dou3 ge3 waa2 gei3 dak1 send go3 message bei2 ngo5
rounds.translation: If you’re running late, remember to send me a message.

chunks.note: 嘅話 at the end of a clause means if.

chunks.jyutping: gei3 dak1 send go3 message bei2 ngo5
chunks.english: remember to send me a message
chunks.note: 畀我 at the end means to me.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask them to message you if they’re late.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: If you’re running late, remember to send me a message.

lessons.summary: Handle a bad phone line, then leave a voice message asking a friend to call back.

content.title: Phone and voice messages
content.scenario: Handle a bad phone line, then leave a voice message asking a friend to call back.

rounds.situation: You call your friend Ming. Someone picks up.
rounds.jyutping: wai2 hai6 mai6 aa3 ming4 aa3
rounds.translation: Hello, is that Ming?

chunks.note: 喂 is only for the phone or calling someone over.
阿 before a name sounds friendly.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Answer the call and check it’s Ming.

rounds.situation: The line is crackly.
rounds.cantonese: 我聽唔清楚，你講大聲啲。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 teng1 m4 cing1 co2 nei5 gong2 daai6 seng1 di1
rounds.translation: I can’t hear you clearly, speak up a bit.

chunks.note: Verb + 唔 + result: tried but couldn’t.
啲 after an adjective means a bit more.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell Ming you can’t hear and ask them to speak up.

rounds.situation: It’s no use. Say you’ll call back.
rounds.jyutping: seon3 hou6 m4 hou2 ngo5 daa2 faan1 bei2 nei5
rounds.translation: The signal’s bad, I’ll call you back.

chunks.note: A perfect excuse in the MTR.
返 means back: 打返 is call back.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Blame the signal and say you’ll call back.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: seon3 hou6 m4 hou2 ngo5 daa2 faan1 bei2 nei5
responseExercise.promptTranslation: The signal’s bad, I’ll call you back.

options.englishTranslation: The signal’s bad, I’ll call you back.
The signal’s good, let’s keep talking.
Hello, is that Ming?

rounds.situation: You call back but nobody answers. Leave a voice message.
rounds.jyutping: tau4 sin1 daa2 bei2 nei5 mou5 jan4 teng1
rounds.translation: I called you just now but nobody picked up.

chunks.note: 頭先 means a moment ago.
Answering the phone is 聽電話: listen to the phone.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Start your voice message.

rounds.situation: Finish the voice message.
rounds.jyutping: dak1 haan4 fuk1 ngo5 din6 waa2 laa1
rounds.translation: Call me back when you’re free.

chunks.note: 得閒 at the start means whenever you have time.
覆電話 means return a call. 啦 keeps it friendly.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask Ming to call you back when free.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: dak1 haan4 fuk1 ngo5 din6 waa2 laa1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Call me back when you’re free.

options.englishTranslation: I’ll call you back when I’m free.

lessons.summary: Describe your symptoms to a doctor and walk out with medicine and a sick note.

content.title: At the doctor
content.scenario: Describe your symptoms to a doctor and walk out with medicine and a sick note.

rounds.situation: You sit down with the doctor.
rounds.jyutping: ji1 sang1 ngo5 m4 syu1 fuk6 loeng5 jat6 laa3
rounds.translation: Doctor, I’ve been feeling unwell for two days.

chunks.note: You can address the doctor simply as 醫生.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 m4 syu1 fuk6 loeng5 jat6 laa3
chunks.english: I’ve been unwell for two days
chunks.note: Duration goes after the state; 喇 means so far.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the doctor how long you’ve been unwell.

rounds.situation: Describe your symptoms.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 tau4 tung3 jau6 jau5 di1 faat3 siu1
rounds.translation: I have a headache and a bit of a fever.

chunks.note: Body part + 痛 = that part hurts.

chunks.english: and a bit of a fever
chunks.note: 有啲 softens it: a bit.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Describe your headache and fever.

rounds.situation: There’s one more thing bothering you.
rounds.cantonese: 喉嚨都好痛，食嘢好辛苦。
rounds.jyutping: hau4 lung4 dou1 hou2 tung3 sik6 je5 hou2 san1 fu2
rounds.translation: My throat really hurts too, eating is hard.

chunks.note: 都 means too, also.
辛苦 is the go-to word for anything tough.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say your throat hurts and eating is hard.

lessons.summary: View a flat with an agent, ask the right questions and negotiate the rent.

content.title: Renting a flat
content.scenario: View a flat with an agent, ask the right questions and negotiate the rent.

rounds.situation: The agent shows you a flat. Ask the rent.
rounds.cantonese: 呢個單位幾多錢一個月？
rounds.jyutping: ni1 go3 daan1 wai2 gei2 do1 cin2 jat1 go3 jyut6
rounds.translation: How much is this flat per month?

chunks.note: Hong Kongers call a flat a 單位, a unit.

chunks.jyutping: gei2 do1 cin2 jat1 go3 jyut6
chunks.note: Price first, then the time period.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask how much the rent is per month.

rounds.situation: Check for hidden costs.
rounds.jyutping: baau1 m4 baau1 gun2 lei5 fai3 gaa3
rounds.translation: Does it include the management fee?

chunks.note: Verb + 唔 + verb makes a yes or no question.
㗎 in a question asks for the facts.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask whether the management fee is included.

rounds.situation: Give your honest opinion of the room.
rounds.cantonese: 間房細咗啲，不過好光猛。
rounds.jyutping: gaan1 fong2 sai3 zo2 di1 bat1 gwo3 hou2 gwong1 maang5
rounds.translation: The room is a bit small, but it’s nice and bright.

chunks.english: the room is a bit small
chunks.note: Adjective + 咗啲 means a bit too much.
光猛 is high praise for a Hong Kong flat.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Give a balanced opinion of the room.

responseExercise.promptCantonese: 間房細咗啲，不過好光猛。
responseExercise.promptJyutping: gaan1 fong2 sai3 zo2 di1 bat1 gwo3 hou2 gwong1 maang5
responseExercise.promptTranslation: The room is a bit small, but it’s nice and bright.

options.englishTranslation: The room is big, but it’s quite dark.
How much is this flat per month?
The room is a bit small, but it’s nice and bright.

rounds.situation: Time to negotiate.
rounds.jyutping: jip6 zyu2 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 peng4 di1 aa3
rounds.translation: Could the landlord make it a bit cheaper?

chunks.note: 業主 is the owner; the agent passes your offer on.

chunks.jyutping: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 peng4 di1 aa3
chunks.english: could it be a bit cheaper
chunks.note: Always ask. Rent is often negotiable.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask if the landlord can lower the rent.

rounds.situation: Make your offer.
rounds.cantonese: 如果平五百蚊，我即刻簽約。
rounds.jyutping: jyu4 gwo2 peng4 ng5 baak3 man1 ngo5 zik1 hak1 cim1 joek3
rounds.translation: If it’s 500 dollars cheaper, I’ll sign right away.

chunks.jyutping: jyu4 gwo2 peng4 ng5 baak3 man1
chunks.note: 蚊 is the everyday word for dollars.
即刻 means immediately. Agents love hearing it.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Offer to sign today for a lower rent.

responseExercise.promptCantonese: 如果平五百蚊，我即刻簽約。
responseExercise.promptJyutping: jyu4 gwo2 peng4 ng5 baak3 man1 ngo5 zik1 hak1 cim1 joek3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: If it’s 500 dollars cheaper, I’ll sign right away.

options.englishTranslation: Could the landlord make it a bit cheaper?
If it’s 500 dollars more, I won’t sign.
If it’s 500 dollars cheaper, I’ll sign right away.

lessons.summary: Make small talk with a colleague and mix English into Cantonese like locals do.

content.title: Office small talk
content.scenario: Make small talk with a colleague and mix English into Cantonese like locals do.

rounds.situation: You arrive at the office and see your colleague.
rounds.jyutping: zou2 san4 nei5 sik6 zo2 zou2 caan1 mei6 aa3
rounds.translation: Morning! Have you had breakfast?

chunks.note: The standard greeting until about noon.

chunks.jyutping: nei5 sik6 zo2 zou2 caan1 mei6 aa3
chunks.note: Asking about food is a caring hello.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet your colleague and ask about breakfast.

rounds.situation: They ask you back. Your morning was chaos.
rounds.cantonese: 我今朝趕住返工，冇得食。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 gon2 zyu6 faan1 gung1 mou5 dak1 sik6
rounds.translation: I was rushing to work this morning, didn’t get to eat.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 gon2 zyu6 faan1 gung1
chunks.english: I was rushing to work this morning
chunks.note: 返工 means go to work; 放工 means finish work.
冇得 + verb: no chance to do it.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Explain why you skipped breakfast.

rounds.situation: Check the schedule.
rounds.jyutping: zan6 gaan1 go3 meeting gei2 dim2 hoi1 ci2
rounds.translation: What time does the meeting start later?

chunks.note: Office Cantonese is full of English nouns.
幾點 asks the hour.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask what time the meeting starts.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: zan6 gaan1 go3 meeting gei2 dim2 hoi1 ci2
responseExercise.promptTranslation: What time does the meeting start later?

options.englishTranslation: What time does the meeting end?
Morning! Have you had breakfast?
What time does the meeting start later?

rounds.situation: You need a minute before chatting more.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 check haa5 email sin1 dang2 zan6 zoi3 king1
rounds.translation: Let me check my email first, we’ll talk in a bit.

chunks.english: let me check my email first
chunks.note: 先 at the end means first, before anything else.
傾 means chat. 傾偈 is a good long chat.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Excuse yourself to check email.

rounds.situation: End of the day. Suggest unwinding together.
rounds.jyutping: fong3 gung1 jat1 cai4 heoi3 jam2 bui1 je5 laa1
rounds.translation: Let’s grab a drink together after work!

chunks.note: 放工 is the best word of the day.

chunks.jyutping: jat1 cai4 heoi3 jam2 bui1 je5 laa1
chunks.note: 飲杯嘢 can be tea, coffee or a beer.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite your colleague for a drink after work.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: fong3 gung1 jat1 cai4 heoi3 jam2 bui1 je5 laa1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Let’s grab a drink together after work!

options.englishTranslation: Let me check my email first, we’ll talk in a bit.
Let’s grab a drink together after work!
Let’s have lunch together tomorrow!

lessons.summary: Visit relatives for Lunar New Year: greetings, red packets and a lucky pun.

content.title: Lunar New Year
content.scenario: Visit relatives for Lunar New Year: greetings, red packets and a lucky pun.

rounds.situation: You arrive at your auntie’s place for New Year.
rounds.jyutping: gung1 hei2 faat3 coi4 san1 tai2 gin6 hong1
rounds.translation: Happy New Year, and good health!

chunks.note: Literally may you get rich. Say it to everyone.
The perfect add-on for older relatives.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet your auntie for the New Year.

rounds.situation: Your auntie hands you a red packet.
rounds.jyutping: do1 ze6 gu1 maa1 ge3 lai6 si6
rounds.translation: Thanks for the red packet, Auntie!

chunks.note: Use 多謝 for gifts, 唔該 for services.
Take it with both hands.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Thank your auntie for the red packet.

rounds.situation: Your auntie teases you about getting married.
rounds.jyutping: gam1 nin2 ngo5 dou1 jiu3 paai3 lai6 si6 laa3
rounds.translation: This year I have to give out red packets too.

chunks.english: this year I also have to
chunks.note: Once you’re married, you give instead of receive.
喇 marks the sad change of status.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Joke that you have to give red packets now.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: gam1 nin2 ngo5 dou1 jiu3 paai3 lai6 si6 laa3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: This year I have to give out red packets too.

options.englishTranslation: This year I have to give out red packets too.
Thanks for the red packet, Auntie!
This year I can collect lots of red packets.

rounds.situation: Tell your auntie your plans for the holiday.
rounds.cantonese: 初二我哋返婆婆屋企拜年。
rounds.jyutping: co1 ji6 ngo5 dei6 faan1 po4 po2 uk1 kei2 baai3 nin4
rounds.translation: On the second day, we’re visiting Grandma’s for New Year.

chunks.jyutping: co1 ji6 ngo5 dei6 faan1 po4 po2 uk1 kei2
chunks.english: on day two we go back to Grandma’s home
chunks.note: Day two is traditionally for visiting mum’s side.
拜年 means visiting relatives with greetings.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say where you’ll visit on the second day.

rounds.situation: Offer your auntie some New Year cake with a lucky pun.
rounds.jyutping: sik6 do1 gin6 nin4 gou1 bou6 bou6 gou1 sing1
rounds.translation: Have another piece of New Year cake, and keep rising higher!

chunks.english: have another piece of New Year cake
chunks.note: 糕 sounds like 高, high. That’s the joke.
A wish for promotions and success.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Offer New Year cake with the lucky wish.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: sik6 do1 gin6 nin4 gou1 bou6 bou6 gou1 sing1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Have another piece of New Year cake, and keep rising higher!

options.englishTranslation: On the second day, we’re visiting Grandma’s for New Year.
Happy New Year, and good health!
Have another piece of New Year cake, and keep rising higher!

lessons.summary: Sort out a wrong order at a restaurant, politely but firmly.

content.title: Something went wrong
content.scenario: Sort out a wrong order at a restaurant, politely but firmly.

rounds.situation: The waiter puts down a dish you didn’t order.
rounds.cantonese: 唔好意思，我冇叫呢碟嘢喎。
rounds.jyutping: m4 hou2 ji3 si1 ngo5 mou5 giu3 ni1 dip6 je5 wo3
rounds.translation: Sorry, I didn’t order this dish.

chunks.note: A soft sorry to open a complaint politely.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 mou5 giu3 ni1 dip6 je5 wo3
chunks.note: 喎 gently points out something they missed.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Politely say this isn’t your dish.

rounds.situation: Say what you actually ordered.
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 giu3 ge3 hai6 gon1 caau2 ngau4 ho2
rounds.translation: What I ordered was beef chow fun.

chunks.note: Verb + 嘅 makes the thing I ordered.
A Cantonese classic. Worth fighting for.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the waiter what you ordered.

rounds.situation: Ask if there’s been a mix-up.
rounds.jyutping: hai6 mai6 gaau2 co3 zo2 aa3
rounds.translation: Has there been a mix-up?

chunks.note: 係咪 makes it a question without blaming anyone.
搞錯 is a mistake. Very handy.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask whether there’s been a mix-up.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: hai6 mai6 gaau2 co3 zo2 aa3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Has there been a mix-up?

options.englishTranslation: Has the food arrived yet?
Has there been a mix-up?
Sorry, I didn’t order this dish.

rounds.situation: Twenty minutes later, still no noodles.
rounds.cantonese: 等咗廿分鐘，可唔可以快啲呀？
rounds.jyutping: dang2 zo2 jaa6 fan1 zung1 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 faai3 di1 aa3
rounds.translation: We’ve waited twenty minutes, could it be a bit faster?

chunks.note: 廿 is the spoken way to say twenty.

chunks.jyutping: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 faai3 di1 aa3
chunks.english: could it be a bit faster
chunks.note: Firm but polite. 呀 keeps it friendly.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Politely ask them to hurry.

rounds.situation: The right dish finally arrives with an apology.
rounds.jyutping: m4 gan2 jiu3 m4 goi1 saai3
rounds.translation: No worries, thanks so much!

chunks.note: The kindest way to accept an apology.
晒 makes 唔該 extra warm.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Accept the apology and thank the waiter.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: m4 gan2 jiu3 m4 goi1 saai3
responseExercise.promptTranslation: No worries, thanks so much!

options.englishTranslation: No worries, thanks so much!

Never mind, I’ll eat somewhere else!
